title: What If You Could See All of the Andromeda Galaxy?

scenes.text: What if your eyes were stronger? Andromeda would span the sky like six full moons.
It's the nearest big galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away.
Its disk is about 140,000 light-years across, and that size is why it looks so wide.
That makes it more than three degrees wide. The Moon is only half a degree.
Today you only see its bright core, a faint smudge, from a dark site.
It's the farthest thing most people can see with no telescope. And it's huge. Your eyes are the limit.

description:
What if you could see the whole Andromeda galaxy?
It spans more than three degrees, roughly six full moons, but only its core is bright enough to see.
